text:
Today we're going to show you
how to take your blood pressure at home.
Hello, I'm Emily,

a Senior Cardiac Nurse
at the British Heart Foundation.
To make sure your blood pressure

reading is accurate, it's important
that you feel relaxed and not stressed.

Please take at least 5 minutes to rest
before checking your blood pressure.
Sit upright with your back

against the back of the chair
and rest your feet flat on the floor.

Rest your arm on a table
and make sure your hand is relaxed.
Don't clench your fist.

You can measure your blood pressure
on either arm,
just remember to always use the same one.

Place the cuff over your upper arm,
just above the bend of your elbow
and not over clothing.

The tube should run down the center
of the front of your arm
or slightly to the right.
Tighten the cuff around your arm,

but make sure you can still fit
2 fingers underneath.
Don't talk.
Press the on button.

You'll feel the cuff quickly
inflate and deflate,

which may feel a bit uncomfortable,
but it's only for a short while.
Your reading will show.

Most blood pressure monitors
save your readings.
If yours doesn't, write it down.
If your cuff is too uncomfortable,

just press the stop button
and the cuff will immediately deflate.

It's a good idea to check your blood
pressure again a few minutes
later to check that
the readings are similar and accurate.

It's normal for the second
reading to be slightly lower.

If you've been asked by your GP
to check your blood pressure, check it

twice a day, once in the morning
and once an evening.
If your blood pressure reading is high

or you're not sure what it should be,
please be to your GP or pharmacist.
